The visible hunks are entirely test additions that encode expected VPlan recipe sequences for tail folding, vp intrinsics, reductions, reverse iteration, and widening calls, without changing production vectorizer code in the retrieved snippets.
Changed symbols: vplan-vp-intrinsics-fixed-order-recurrence.ll; vplan-riscv-vector-reverse.ll; vplan-force-tail-with-evl.ll; sve-tail-folding-forced.ll; sve2-histcnt-vplan.ll; widen-call-with-intrinsic-or-libfunc.ll; vplan-vp-intrinsics-reduction.ll; vplan-printing.ll
Behavioral change: Adds regression coverage for VPlan printing and recipe ordering in multiple vectorization scenarios.; Documents expected ordering of phi-like, widening, and intrinsic recipes in debug output.; Does not show any code-path change in the retrieved hunks.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; LoopVectorize; phi-like recipe; recipe ordering; debug-only=loop-vectorize
Reproducer link: The tests exercise vectorization debug output for several loops, including tail folding and vp intrinsics.; They are consistent with the issue domain but do not demonstrate a fix or regression in code.
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan printing tests; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan

But the retrieved hunks are test-only, so there is no direct behavioral change in the compiler implementation to causally explain or fix the assertion. It is useful evidence of subsystem focus, not of the bug source itself.

+; IF-EVL: <x1> vector loop: {
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:   vector.body:
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[IV:%[0-9]+]]> = CANONICAL-INDUCTION
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EXPLICIT-VECTOR-LENGTH-BASED-IV-PHI vp<[[EVL_PHI:%[0-9]+]]> = phi ir<0>, vp<[[IV_NEXT:%.+]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     FIRST-ORDER-RECURRENCE-PHI ir<[[FOR_PHI:%.+]]> = phi ir<33>, ir<[[LD:%.+]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[AVL:%.+]]> = phi [ ir<%TC>, vector.ph ], [ vp<[[AVL_NEXT:%.+]]>, vector.body ]
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[PREV_EVL:%.+]]> = phi [ vp<[[VF32]]>, vector.ph ], [ vp<[[EVL:%.+]]>, vector.body ]
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[EVL]]> = EXPLICIT-VECTOR-LENGTH vp<[[AVL]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     vp<[[ST:%[0-9]+]]> = SCALAR-STEPS vp<[[EVL_PHI]]>, ir<1>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     CLONE ir<[[GEP1:%.+]]> = getelementptr inbounds nuw ir<%A>, vp<[[ST]]
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     vp<[[PTR1:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-pointer inbounds nuw ir<[[GEP1]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     WIDEN ir<[[LD]]> = vp.load vp<[[PTR1]]>, vp<[[EVL]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     WIDEN-INTRINSIC vp<[[SPLICE:%[0-9]+]]> = call llvm.experimental.vp.splice(ir<[[FOR_PHI]]>, ir<[[LD]]>, ir<-1>, ir<true>, vp<[[PREV_EVL]]>, vp<[[EVL]]>)
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     WIDEN ir<[[ADD:%.+]]> = add nsw vp<[[SPLICE]]>, ir<[[LD]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     CLONE ir<[[GEP2:%.+]]> = getelementptr inbounds nuw ir<%B>, vp<[[ST]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     vp<[[PTR2:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-pointer inbounds nuw ir<[[GEP2]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     WIDEN vp.store vp<[[PTR2]]>, ir<[[ADD]]>, vp<[[EVL]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT-SCALAR vp<[[CAST:%[0-9]+]]> = zext vp<[[EVL]]> to i64
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[IV_NEXT]]> = add vp<[[CAST]]>, vp<[[EVL_PHI]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[AVL_NEXT]]> = sub nuw vp<[[AVL]]>, vp<[[CAST]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[IV_NEXT_EXIT:%.+]]> = add vp<[[IV]]>, vp<[[VFUF]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:     EMIT branch-on-count  vp<[[IV_NEXT_EXIT]]>, vp<[[VTC]]>
+; IF-EVL-NEXT:   No successors
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: }
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Successor(s): middle.block
+; IF-EVL-EMPTY:
+; IF-EVL: middle.block:
+; IF-EVL-NEXT: Successor(s): ir-bb<for.end>
+
+; IF-EVL: Cost of 0 for VF vscale x 4: FIRST-ORDER-RECURRENCE-PHI ir<[[FOR_PHI]]> = phi ir<33>, ir<[[LD]]>
+; IF-EVL: Cost of 4 for VF vscale x 4: WIDEN-INTRINSIC vp<[[SPLICE]]> = call llvm.experimental.vp.splice(ir<[[FOR_PHI]]>, ir<[[LD]]>, ir<-1>, ir<true>, vp<[[PREV_EVL]]>, vp<[[EVL]]>)
+entry:
+  br label %for.body
+
+for.body:
+  %indvars = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %indvars.next, %for.body ]

+  %arrayidx = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr %A, i64 %indvars

+; RUN: opt -passes=loop-vectorize -debug-only=loop-vectorize \

+; RUN: -mcpu=pwr10 -disable-output < %s 2>&1 | FileCheck %s

+define void @foo(ptr noalias %a, ptr noalias %b, ptr noalias %c, i64 %N) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={2,4},UF>=1' {
+; CHECK-NEXT: Live-in vp<[[VF:%.+]]> = VF
+; CHECK-NEXT: Live-in vp<[[VFxUF:%.+]]> = VF * UF
+; CHECK-NEXT: Live-in vp<[[VTC:%.+]]> = vector-trip-count
+; CHECK-NEXT: Live-in vp<[[BTC:%.+]]> = backedge-taken count
+; CHECK-NEXT: Live-in ir<%N> = original trip-count
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT: ir-bb<entry>:
+; CHECK-NEXT: Successor(s): scalar.ph, vector.ph
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT: vector.ph:
+; CHECK-NEXT: Successor(s): vector loop
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT: <x1> vector loop: {
+; CHECK-NEXT:   vector.body:
+; CHECK-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[CAN_IV:%.+]]> = CANONICAL-INDUCTION ir<0>, vp<[[CAN_INC:%.*]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:     ir<%iv> = WIDEN-INDUCTION ir<0>, ir<1>, vp<[[VF]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[CMP:%.+]]> = icmp ule ir<%iv>, vp<[[BTC]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:   Successor(s): pred.store
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT:  <xVFxUF> pred.store: {
+; CHECK-NEXT:    pred.store.entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:      BRANCH-ON-MASK vp<[[CMP]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:    Successor(s): pred.store.if, pred.store.continue
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    pred.store.if:
+; CHECK-NEXT:      vp<[[STEPS:%.+]]> = SCALAR-STEPS vp<[[CAN_IV]]>, ir<1>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      REPLICATE ir<%arrayidx> = getelementptr inbounds ir<%b>, vp<[[STEPS]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      REPLICATE ir<%0> = load ir<%arrayidx>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      REPLICATE ir<%arrayidx2> = getelementptr inbounds ir<%c>, vp<[[STEPS]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      REPLICATE ir<%1> = load ir<%arrayidx2>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      REPLICATE ir<%arrayidx4> = getelementptr inbounds ir<%a>, vp<[[STEPS]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      REPLICATE ir<%add> = add nsw ir<%1>, ir<%0>
+; CHECK-NEXT:      REPLICATE store ir<%add>, ir<%arrayidx4>
+; CHECK-NEXT:    Successor(s): pred.store.continue
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    pred.store.continue:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    No successors
+; CHECK-NEXT:  }
+; CHECK-NEXT:  Successor(s): for.body.2
+; CHECK-EMPTY:
+; CHECK-NEXT:  for.body.2:
+; CHECK-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[CAN_INC:%.+]]> = add vp<[[CAN_IV]]>, vp<[[VFxUF]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:     EMIT branch-on-count vp<[[CAN_INC]]>, vp<[[VTC]]>
+; CHECK-NEXT:   No successors
+; CHECK-NEXT: }
+;
+entry:
+  br label %for.body
+
+for.body:
+  %iv = phi i64 [ 0, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %for.body ]

+  %1 = load i32, ptr %arrayidx2, align 4

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/AArch64/sve-tail-folding-forced.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/AArch64/sve-tail-folding-forced.ll

+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/VPlan/AArch64/sve-tail-folding-forced.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --filter-out-after "^scalar.ph:"
+; RUN: opt -S -passes=loop-vectorize -debug-only=loop-vectorize < %s 2>%t | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: cat %t | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=VPLANS
+
+; These tests ensure that tail-folding is enabled when the predicate.enable
+; loop attribute is set to true.
+
+target triple = "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu"
+
+; VPLANS-LABEL: Checking a loop in 'simple_memset'
+; VPLANS:      VPlan 'Initial VPlan for VF={vscale x 1,vscale x 2,vscale x 4},UF>=1' {
+; VPLANS-NEXT: Live-in vp<[[VF:%.+]]> = VF
+; VPLANS-NEXT: Live-in vp<[[VFxUF:%.+]]> = VF * UF
+; VPLANS:      vp<[[TC:%[0-9]+]]> = original trip-count
+; VPLANS-EMPTY:
+; VPLANS-NEXT: ir-bb<entry>:
+; VPLANS-NEXT:  EMIT vp<[[TC]]> = EXPAND SCEV (1 umax %n)
+; VPLANS-NEXT: Successor(s): scalar.ph, vector.ph
+; VPLANS-EMPTY:
+; VPLANS-NEXT: vector.ph:
+; VPLANS-NEXT:   EMIT vp<[[NEWTC:%[0-9]+]]> = TC > VF ? TC - VF : 0 vp<[[TC]]>
+; VPLANS-NEXT:   EMIT vp<[[VF_PER_PART:%.+]]> = VF * Part + ir<0>
+; VPLANS-NEXT:   EMIT vp<[[LANEMASK_ENTRY:%.+]]> = active lane mask vp<[[VF_PER_PART]]>, vp<[[TC]]>
+; VPLANS-NEXT: Successor(s): vector loop
+; VPLANS-EMPTY:
+; VPLANS-NEXT: <x1> vector loop: {
+; VPLANS-NEXT:   vector.body:
+; VPLANS-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[INDV:%[0-9]+]]> = CANONICAL-INDUCTION
+; VPLANS-NEXT:     ACTIVE-LANE-MASK-PHI vp<[[LANEMASK_PHI:%[0-9]+]]> = phi vp<[[LANEMASK_ENTRY]]>, vp<[[LANEMASK_LOOP:%.+]]>
+; VPLANS-NEXT:     vp<[[STEP:%[0-9]+]]>    = SCALAR-STEPS vp<[[INDV]]>, ir<1>, vp<[[VF]]>
+; VPLANS-NEXT:     CLONE ir<%gep> = getelementptr ir<%ptr>, vp<[[STEP]]>
+; VPLANS-NEXT:     vp<[[VEC_PTR:%[0-9]+]]> = vector-pointer ir<%gep>
+; VPLANS-NEXT:     WIDEN store vp<[[VEC_PTR]]>, ir<%val>, vp<[[LANEMASK_PHI]]>
+; VPLANS-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[INDV_UPDATE:%.+]]> = add vp<[[INDV]]>, vp<[[VFxUF]]>
+; VPLANS-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[INC:%[0-9]+]]> = VF * Part + vp<[[INDV]]>
+; VPLANS-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[LANEMASK_LOOP]]> = active lane mask vp<[[INC]]>, vp<[[NEWTC]]>
+; VPLANS-NEXT:     EMIT vp<[[NOT:%[0-9]+]]> = not vp<[[LANEMASK_LOOP]]>
+; VPLANS-NEXT:     EMIT branch-on-cond vp<[[NOT]]>
+; VPLANS-NEXT:   No successors
+; VPLANS-NEXT: }
+
+define void @simple_memset(i32 %val, ptr %ptr, i64 %n) #0 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: @simple_memset(
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[UMAX:%.*]] = call i64 @llvm.umax.i64(i64 [[N:%.*]], i64 1)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[VECTOR_PH:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       vector.ph:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP13:%.*]] = call i64 @llvm.vscale.i64()
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP14:%.*]] = shl nuw i64 [[TMP13]], 2
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP5:%.*]] = call i64 @llvm.vscale.i64()

steps.subject: [VPlan] Optimize FindLast of (binop %IV, live-in) by sinking. (#183911)

evidence: Directly changes VPlanTransforms and LoopVectorize recipe/value construction in a sinking optimization path.
Introduces new sinking/cloning behavior and alters middle-block select/reduction construction, which is closer to ordering-sensitive VPlan bugs than the other candidates.
features: LoopVectorize reduction handling, VPlanTransforms, expression sinking, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize, path:llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This patch extends VPlan's optimizeFindIVReductions to sink expressions derived from widened IVs and to use the vector-region exiting value rather than the reduced IV in the middle-block select/any-of construction. It also adds logic to detect a sinkable expression IV, clone the expression into the loop, and update the backedge/select handling accordingly. The accompanying tests show changed epilogue and reduction shapes for sinkable IV expressions.
Changed symbols: llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize/VPlanTransforms.cpp::VPlanTransforms::optimizeFindIVReductions; getExpressionIV; vputils::getSCEVExprForVPValue; cloneBinOpForScalarIV; VPBuilder; createSelect; createNaryOp
Behavioral change: Tracks the underlying IV for sinkable expressions instead of only the expression itself.; Creates a new select that uses the underlying IV directly when sinking is possible.; Substitutes the vector-region exiting value into reduction-result construction, changing the recipe/value ordering in the middle block.
Assertion or trace link: VPlan; LoopVectorize; recipe ordering; phi-like recipe
Reproducer link: find-last IV sinkable expression epilogue/vectorization patterns; changed vector body and middle block IR shape

top_candidates.subject: [VPlan] Simplify add x, (sub 0, y) -> sub x, y (#187228)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit simplifies VPlan arithmetic canonicalization by rewriting patterns of add x, (sub 0, y) into sub x, y, preserving nsw flags when possible. The change is reflected in multiple LoopVectorize tests that now expect subtraction forms instead of add-with-negation sequences.
Changed symbols: simplifyRecipe; VPSingleDefRecipe; VPRecipeWithIRFlags; Builder.createSub
Behavioral change: Introduces a new VPlan simplification rule that canonicalizes add of a negated operand into a subtraction recipe.; Preserves no-signed-wrap semantics on the rewritten subtraction when both original operations had nsw.; Changes the shape of generated VPlan recipes and resulting IR from add/sub-zero patterns to direct sub instructions.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; recipe ordering; phi-like recipe
Reproducer link: vector-reverse and induction-related vectorization test shape changes; codegen differences in induction updates and reverse loops
Pass or subsystem link: VPlanTransforms; LoopVectorize
Causal explanation: This commit is in the right subsystem and changes recipe creation/simplification, which can influence VPlan ordering indirectly. But the retrieved hunk is specifically about arithmetic canonicalization, and the visible evidence does not mention phi-like recipes, canonical IV placement, or the asserted ordering invariant. The connection to the reported crash is therefore weak.
Causal confidence: 0.28
Build risk: High-risk path: llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize/VPlanTransforms.cpp; Multiple LoopVectorize test expectation updates; Affects recipe simplification and IR flag propagation

top_candidates.subject: [LV] Remove IV use restrictions for epilogue vectorization. (#190552)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change removes a precondition in LoopVectorize's epilogue-vectorization candidate selection that rejected induction variables with uses outside the loop. The deleted code had explicitly filtered out phis whose post-increment or penultimate induction values were used by instructions outside the original loop, so epilogue vectorization can now proceed for more loops with live-out IV-related uses.
Changed symbols: LoopVectorizationPlanner::isCandidateForEpilogueVectorization; Legal->getInductionVars; OrigLoop->getLoopLatch
Behavioral change: Drops the check that disallowed epilogue vectorization when induction-variable values have uses outside the loop.; Allows loops with live-out induction-related uses to be considered for epilogue vectorization instead of bailing out early.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize/VPlan assertion; Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe; phi-like recipe ordering
Reproducer link: crash at -O3 on crash-62b480.cpp; LoopVectorize/VPlan plan construction during vectorization
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; epilogue vectorization
Causal explanation: The issue is an assertion about VPlan recipe ordering, not directly about IV-use legality. However, this patch broadens the set of loops that reach epilogue-vectorization planning, including loops with live-out induction uses, which is plausibly related to the crash surface. The retrieved hunks do not show any direct recipe-ordering fix, so the link is indirect and evidence is limited.
Causal confidence: 0.42
Build risk: Touches high-risk LoopVectorize control flow; Changes epilogue-vectorization eligibility; Associated tests update expected vectorization shape for live-out IV cases

Summary: This change tightens the AArch64 partial-reduction profitability gate so partial reductions are chosen only when strictly cheaper than the regular reduction path. It also updates multiple LoopVectorize AArch64 tests to reflect altered vectorization and reduction materialization decisions, including wider vector phis and different reduction lowering.
Changed symbols: VPlanTransforms::createPartialReductions; VPlanTransforms.cpp; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/partial-reduce.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/partial-reduce-usabs.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/partial-reduce-fdot-product.ll

Affects vector trip-count materialization and can alter VPlan shape, but the diff does not directly touch phi-like recipe ordering or the asserted recipe sequence.
features: LoopVectorize, VPlanTransforms, meta:core-llvm, path:llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize, path:llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize, plan construction
selection.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit extends LoopVectorize/VPlan trip-count materialization with a maximum runtime step estimate derived from scalable VF/UF and uses it to simplify vector trip-count construction when the scalar trip count is a constant divisible by that maximum step. It also threads the new optional parameter through the planner and updates tests to reflect removed modulo-based trip-count code in some scalable-vector cases.
Changed symbols: LoopVectorizationPlanner::executePlan; VPlanTransforms::materializeVectorTripCount; VPlanTransforms::materializeVectorTripCount (declaration); llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/simple_early_exit.ll; llvm/test/Transforms/LoopVectorize/AArch64/sve-epilog-vect.ll
Behavioral change: Computes an optional MaxRuntimeStep from max vscale, VF, and UF in the planner.; MaterializeVectorTripCount can now bypass generating a runtime remainder when the trip count is a constant divisible by the maximum possible step.; This changes vector-trip-count construction for scalable VFs and can remove urem/sub sequences in the generated IR.
Assertion or trace link: LoopVectorize; VPlan; vector trip count; recipe construction
Reproducer link: clang crashes at -O3; VPlan recipe ordering assertion involving phi-like recipes
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; VPlanTransforms; VPlan
Causal explanation: The patch is in the same LoopVectorize/VPlan area as the issue and changes plan construction logic, but the retrieved hunks only affect vector trip-count materialization for scalable vectors. There is no direct evidence here about phi-like recipe ordering, recipe insertion order, or the specific assertion. The connection is therefore indirect: it may alter VPlan shape, but the hunks do not show the ordering bug itself.
Causal confidence: 0.31
Build risk: High-risk path: llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize/LoopVectorize.cpp; High-risk path: llvm/lib/Transforms/Vectorize/VPlanTransforms.cpp; Behavioral change in scalable-vector code generation; Associated test expectation updates in AArch64 LoopVectorize tests

The patch replaces a pair-tracking set with direct inspection of the PHI scalars and adds a bailout when an instruction has users outside the grandparent PHI's scalar set, preserving scheduler dependency accounting. The change is in LLVM vectorization, but specifically SLP scheduling rather than LoopVectorize/VPlan.
Changed symbols: BoUpSLP::BlockScheduling::tryScheduleBundle; SLPVectorizer.cpp

top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This BOLT change adds a regression test for split DWARF DWP processing when an unexpected section such as .debug_line.dwo is present, documenting and guarding against a null pointer dereference in getSliceData/getContribution. The retrieved material is entirely in BOLT debug-section handling tests and does not modify LLVM vectorization or VPlan code.
Changed symbols: getSliceData; getContribution; bolt/test/X86/dwarf4-dwp-x86.s
Behavioral change: Adds a test case ensuring BOLT does not crash when a DWP file contains a section kind not tracked in the CU index.; Captures a null-pointer-dereference scenario in split DWARF debug processing.
Assertion or trace link: Found phi-like recipe after non-phi recipe; LoopVectorize; VPlan
Reproducer link: crash during BOLT update-debug-sections with split DWARF; null pointer dereference in getSliceData()
Pass or subsystem link: BOLT; split DWARF / DWP processing; debug section handling
Causal explanation: The evidence points to a BOLT debug-info crash, not the LoopVectorize/VPlan assertion from the issue. Since the patch only adds a BOLT test and does not alter LLVM's vectorizer or recipe ordering logic, it is unrelated to the reported crash in the available hunks.
Causal confidence: 0.99
Build risk: Test-only change in BOLT; No optimizer or vectorizer code touched; Crash signature and subsystem differ from the reported LoopVectorize assertion

diff --git a/bolt/test/X86/dwarf4-dwp-x86.s b/bolt/test/X86/dwarf4-dwp-x86.s
index 6dde1678f384..a2839e7b9c27 100755
--- a/bolt/test/X86/dwarf4-dwp-x86.s
+++ b/bolt/test/X86/dwarf4-dwp-x86.s
@@ -7 +7,11 @@
-
+## Test that BOLT does not crash when a DWP file contains a section (e.g.
+## .debug_line.dwo) whose kind is not tracked as a column in the CU index.
+## This triggers a null pointer dereference in getSliceData() where
+## getContribution() returns nullptr because the section kind has no column.
+# RUN: rm -rf %t && mkdir -p %t && cd %t
+# RUN: split-file %p/dwarf4-dwp-x86.s %t
+# RUN: %clangxx %cxxflags -g -gdwarf-4 -gsplit-dwarf %t/main.s %t/callee.s -o %t/main.exe
+# RUN: llvm-dwp -e %t/main.exe -o %t/main.exe.dwp
+# RUN: printf '\x00' > %t/line.bin
+# RUN: llvm-objcopy --add-section=.debug_line.dwo=%t/line.bin %t/main.exe.dwp
+# RUN: llvm-bolt %t/main.exe -o %t/main.exe.bolt -update-debug-sections  2>&1 | FileCheck %s
